evals.prompt:
Rewrite the existing commit message quoted below using these complete supplied facts. Create a new result.md file containing your rewritten message; draft only, no network or Git operations. This commit changes 18 files. Previously each export caller encoded CSV headers and rows. Now src/export-format.ts defines the formatting contract and src/csv-format.ts owns CSV header and row encoding, so another format can be added without duplicating encoding across callers. The remaining files migrate callers and test encoding. CSV remains the only format and the default; escaping, column order, and newline behavior remain unchanged. No test execution result is supplied. Existing message: refactor(export): centralize CSV formatting

Export callers previously each encoded CSV headers and rows. CSV headers and rows were therefore encoded in each caller. Introducing another format would require encoding changes in callers. This is why the formatting boundary matters.

src/export-format.ts defines the formatting contract. The contract is the place where callers connect to format-specific encoding. It is a common contract for formatting. src/csv-format.ts owns CSV header and row encoding. Headers and rows are both handled by the CSV implementation.

Other changed files migrate callers and test encoding. Callers now use the formatting contract. The encoding tests cover encoding behavior. Separating encoding makes it possible to add another format without duplicating encoding across callers. No second format is added here.

CSV remains the only format. CSV remains the default. Escaping is unchanged. Column order is unchanged. Newline behavior is unchanged. These preserved properties mean the formatting refactor preserves these aspects of CSV output.

Suggested review order: start with src/export-format.ts for the contract. Then read src/csv-format.ts for header and row encoding. Then inspect callers and encoding tests. The main question is whether another format can be added without spreading encoding across callers.

In summary, this centralizes formatting while retaining CSV as the default and only format, with escaping, column order, and newlines unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A clear, accurate message with comparable reading effort to the paired case for the same change; evaluate cases 10 and 11 together for length anchoring.
expectations: Explains the moved encoding and why the contract enables another format without claiming one was added
Preserves CSV as the only/default format and unchanged escaping, column order, and newline behavior without inventing test results
